newsitem.title: USA: CPI overstates food-price inflation --USDA analyst.
newsitem.headline: CPI overstates food-price inflation --USDA analyst.

text.p: Evidence suggests that there may be something "systematically incorrect" with the Consumer Price Index for Food at Home, and that the measure could have been off for more than a decade, an Agriculture Department analyst said in an article released Wednesday.

"Analyses by BLS (Bureau of Labor Statistics) and USDA's Economic Research service suggest that the CPI for Food at Home overstates inflation of food prices, and that the gap could be as high as 1 to 1.9 percentage points per year beginning around 1978," wrote USDA analyst James MacDonald.
The article was published in USDA's quarterly Food Review.
